answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit bond tied to one hardware attestation key in the plume registry, which rejects a second identity on the same device. juniper auditors sample devices each epoch and verify keys and outputs match one machine; a mismatch burns the bond and removes the identity. The k-th fake still needs a new device plus 70 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 70,000 credits plus 1,000 devices. A rented device farm fails because shared attestation batches cluster at the wharf checkpoint, where clusters are published and slashed. An honest agent pays 70 once, refundable after a clean epoch.
